# BlinkSend

> Fast, free, peer-to-peer file sharing between phones and computers. No account needed.

Repository: https://github.com/ghostySRC/BlinkSend
Default branch: main
License: MIT
Runtime: Node.js 20+, browser JavaScript, WebRTC data channels

## What BlinkSend does

BlinkSend transfers files directly between two browsers. A small Node.js server handles room signaling, QR generation, temporary ICE/TURN credentials, and static assets. File bytes normally travel peer-to-peer over an encrypted WebRTC data channel rather than through the BlinkSend application server.

## Main capabilities

- Send / Receive entry flow
- QR and invite-link pairing
- mutual six-digit peer verification derived from WebRTC DTLS fingerprints
- incremental SHA-256 file verification
- numbered chunks and reconnect/resume
- restart-safe resume on supported browsers using IndexedDB + persistent file handles
- large-file streaming with File System Access API or OPFS fallback
- folder transfer and nested folder reconstruction on supported browsers
- direct link sharing
- English and Swedish UI
- light/dark themes
- TURN support with short-lived credentials
- server-side rate limiting and malformed signaling controls

## Important files

- README.md — setup, architecture, features, deployment, limitations
- SECURITY.md — threat model and vulnerability reporting
- server.js — HTTP server, WebSocket signaling, room handling, ICE/TURN endpoint, abuse controls
- public/index.html — browser UI structure
- public/app.js — pairing, WebRTC, transfer protocol, resume, folder handling, UI state
- public/sha256.js — incremental SHA-256 implementation used for file integrity
- public/persistence.js — IndexedDB-backed persistent transfer session metadata
- public/style.css — UI styling
- test/signaling.test.js — server/signaling/security tests
- test/sha256.test.js — SHA-256 known-vector tests
- test/client-syntax.test.js — browser-script syntax checks
- .github/workflows/ci.yml — CI

## Development

```bash
npm ci
npm test
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000.

## Architecture

1. Browser A joins a random room.
2. Browser B joins the same room.
3. server.js forwards WebRTC SDP/ICE signaling only.
4. Browsers establish a WebRTC data channel.
5. Both users compare and confirm the same six-digit verification code.
6. File data is split into numbered chunks and sent over WebRTC.
7. Receiver hashes incoming bytes with SHA-256.
8. Sender and receiver compare hashes before reporting a verified transfer.
9. Interrupted transfers can resume from the receiver's next committed chunk.
10. Supported browsers persist transfer state and file handles for reload-safe resume.

## Security notes

Room URLs are bearer secrets and should be shared privately. Peer verification is required before transfer controls unlock. TURN credentials are short-lived and require a valid room join token. File integrity is checked end-to-end with SHA-256. Public production deployments should still use edge/reverse-proxy rate limiting and TURN bandwidth controls.

## Browser capability notes

Some features depend on browser support:
- showOpenFilePicker / showSaveFilePicker
- showDirectoryPicker
- persistent FileSystemHandle objects in IndexedDB
- OPFS

Fallbacks are kept where possible.

## AI / coding-agent guidance

Read README.md, SECURITY.md, server.js, public/app.js, public/persistence.js, and the tests before making protocol changes.
Do not remove peer verification, SHA-256 validation, room limits, signaling validation, or rate limits.
Keep the user-facing flow simple and account-free.
Prefer small compatible protocol changes and update tests and README when behavior changes.
